summary: A large anchored two-star packet in the current O0 effective-dimension-two near-coloop branch does not force a genuine two-cross block after putting the two anchors on one physical side. For K=100, a target-class symmetric matrix has L|R cross singular values K,K,1,1,1, E3=3K^4+6K^2+1, both chosen anchor ridge leverages >23/24, anchored two-star mass K^4>E2/2, but the checkerboard {i,j}|rest cross block has two identical rows and E2=0. Full QFORM is not refuted; the same family is paid by the completed rank-five cross-fiber theorem. The valid replacement theorem is QFORM-TWOSTAR-CHECKERBOARD-WEDGE-v1: if the checkerboard E2 is at least eta times the star product, a two-cross half-Riesz estimate pays it; otherwise the two central outside-coupling rows are quantitatively near proportional, with an exact decoupled leaf at E2=0.
